tested_scope.candidate: GitHub REST commit-status objects as a default service-side monotonic/rollback witness coupled to repository Contents-API CAS publication
questions: Whether status records expose create/update/delete semantics compatible with append-only witnessing
Whether IDs or list order are documented as monotonic generation authority
Whether status discovery survives branch/history rewrite when the target commit becomes unreferenced
Dual-write ambiguity between Contents-API CAS publication and status creation
excluded: No commit status was created in the repository
No protected settings, branch protection, Actions, hosted runner, Codespaces, packages, artifacts, cloud credit or richer execution mode was used
GitHub.com retention of unreachable commit/status metadata was not experimentally forced or generalized from Enterprise Server GC documentation

public_sources.source: GitHub Docs - REST API endpoints for commit statuses
observations: The documented commit-status surface consists of get-combined, list-statuses and create-status operations; no status update/delete endpoint is documented on that resource page.
List commit statuses accepts a SHA, branch or tag reference and returns statuses in reverse chronological order with the latest first.

Create commit status requires push access; fine-grained tokens require Commit statuses: write. Listing requires pull access; fine-grained tokens require Commit statuses: read, and public resources can be read without authentication.
Create status is limited to 1000 statuses per sha/context, so repeated creation is explicitly possible rather than a single CAS slot.

public_sources.source: GitHub Docs - removing sensitive data / unreachable Git objects (Enterprise Server public documentation)
observations: Official documentation describes unreachable commits being eligible for garbage collection after references are removed.

This is evidence against assuming a commit-SHA-addressed status remains durably discoverable after arbitrary history rewrite; it is not a GitHub.com retention SLA and therefore supports fail-closed classification rather than a universal deletion claim.

public_sources.source: GitHub Docs - REST API endpoints for Git commit objects
observations: Commit lookup is by commit SHA and can return 404; no retrieved documentation guarantees indefinite lookup after a commit is unreferenced.

bounded_trace_model.witness: S = create commit status on the resulting commit SHA

traces.trace: C succeeds; S succeeds; both responses observed
traces.result: aligned once, but status ID monotonicity/retention is still undocumented, so not an accepted monotonic witness

traces.trace: C succeeds; S fails or is not attempted
traces.result: authoritative content exists without the proposed witness
status can exist for a transition that never became authoritative content

traces.trace: C succeeds; S succeeds; S response is lost; caller retries S
traces.result: create-status has no documented expected-previous-status CAS or idempotency token; duplicate status records are possible up to the documented per-sha/context limit

traces.trace: C succeeds but response is lost before S
traces.result: content can be reconciled by reading current repository state, but a missing status must then be created separately; the witness was not atomic with publication

traces.trace: S succeeds but response is lost before C
traces.result: caller cannot infer authoritative publication from status existence alone; an orphan witness remains possible

traces.trace: both succeed; branch/history later force-rewrites away from target commit
traces.result: status lookup remains commit/ref-addressed; long-term discoverability after the commit becomes unreachable is not proven

traces.trace: status list is read after multiple same-context creates
traces.result: reverse-chronological order identifies latest-by-creation response order, not a documented globally monotonic generation/fencing epoch

bounded_trace_model.result: The candidate fails as a default service-side monotonic rollback witness. Stable transition IDs embedded in both content and status could improve reconciliation of some response-loss cases, but cannot make the two writes atomic, cannot make status IDs a documented monotonic fence, and cannot prove post-rewrite retention/discoverability.

finding.new_falsification: GitHub commit-status objects are create-only at the documented REST status resource, but create-only is not sufficient for monotonic authority. Statuses are attached to a commit SHA/ref, allow repeated creation, expose no documented expected-previous-status CAS/idempotency token, and have no retrieved guarantee that their numeric IDs or survival/discoverability after the target commit becomes unreachable provide a monotonic anti-rollback witness. Separate Contents CAS and status creation therefore retain a dual-write gap.
finding.minimal_unresolved_child: A GitHub-native service-side object whose authority is independently retained/discoverable across branch/history rollback, whose incarnation/order has documented monotonic freshness semantics rather than mere opaque uniqueness/creation order, and whose creation can be atomically coupled to repository publication or deterministically reconciled without duplicate authoritative generations.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.note: This bounded leaf used public documentation and lightweight repository state transport only. Commit statuses were audited, not adopted as coordination authority.

frontier: Audit GitHub pull-request hidden refs / pull-request object identity and retention as the next service-side witness class, focusing on whether ordinary repository authority can erase or rebind the witness and whether a PR ref remains addressable after source-branch force rewrite.

If PR refs are not a durable monotonic witness, test a separate GitHub-native class with documented service-side retention and stable freshness semantics; do not infer append-only behavior from missing delete endpoints alone.
Continue preserving a fail-closed repository-local CAS fallback; unavailable or non-monotonic service-side witnesses remain unresolved children rather than acceptance.
continuation: Part107: execute one bounded public-source leaf on GitHub pull-request hidden refs and pull-request object identity as the next service-side witness class. Audit creation/read/delete/rebind authority, whether refs/pull/* or equivalent service-side commit reachability survives source-branch force rewrite and PR close, discoverability after head commit becomes otherwise unreachable, ID/incarnation freshness semantics, and dual-write ambiguity between repository Contents CAS publication and PR/witness creation. Accept only documented zero-cost, zero-finite-quota, no-richer-mode semantics that prevent stale generation acceptance; otherwise persist the next candidate class without executing it in the same invocation.
